title: Checkpoint: Ring Forensics
prompt:
A ring buffer's public fields live in your editor (`struct ring { int buf[8]; size_t head, tail, count; };`). Implement three verdicts:
1. `bool ring_size_ok(const struct ring *r)` — count <= capacity 8, and head/tail in [0, 8).
2. `bool ring_count_matches(const struct ring *r, size_t expected)` — the recorded count equals the actual occupancy derived from head/tail/count consistency (here: count <= 8 && head < 8 && tail < 8 && (r->count == 0 ? r->head == r->tail : true)).
3. `const char *diagnose(const struct ring *r)` — return "ok" when both verdicts hold; "size-corrupt" when sizes are out of range; "index-corrupt" when head or tail is out of range (checked first).

tests.name: healthy ring
tests.hint: Empty ring, all indices in range: both lattices hold.

tests.name: index corruption diagnosed first
tests.hint: head 9 is outside [0,8) — index verdict fires before size.

tests.name: size corruption
tests.hint: count 9 exceeds capacity 8 with valid indices — size verdict.

tests.name: both corrupt: index wins
tests.hint: head 9 breaks indices AND count 9 breaks size — index is diagnosed first, and both boolean verdicts reject.
